source_text: petis ut ignoscant verecundae aures, et congemiscant potius, quam indignentur necessitati tuae Sed si poterat virile membrum et antea moveri, nihil ergo novitatis invexit delictum
pass_a_gloss: Petis so-that/as ignoscant verecundae ears, and congemiscant rather, than/which indignentur necessitati your but if poterat virile membrum and beforehand moveri, nothing therefore novitatis invexit offense.
pass_b_english: [I ask] modest ears to forgive [me], and to share [my] distress rather than be indignant at [my] necessity.
If the male organ could move before, then sin introduced nothing new.

choices.why: Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
